belief: If my children turn away from God, I failed as a parent.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if your children turn away from God you failed as a parent, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Reading Proverbs 22:6 as a guarantee. Comments from others that blame parents. Regret over mistakes you made while raising your children. Grief over a child who has walked away from faith. Comparing your family with others whose children seem faithful.
teaches: Parents matter, and we are called to raise children in the Lord. But each person makes their own choices. Through Isaiah, God Himself said, “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.” God is the perfect Parent, and His children still rebelled. In Jesus’ story, the prodigal son left a loving father. Proverbs describes wisdom, not a guarantee. God is still at work in your children, and He welcomes prodigals home.
self_statements: It’s my fault my child left the faith.
If I had been a better parent, they’d still believe.
God is disappointed in my parenting.
There’s no hope for my child.
errors: Taking full responsibility for another person’s choices.
Treating a general principle as a guarantee.
Judging your past parenting by what you know now.
Concluding your child will never return.
questions: Did God’s own children rebel against Him?
Was the prodigal’s father a bad parent?
Is Proverbs 22:6 a promise or a general principle?
Does my child have their own choices before God?
What can I still do: pray, love, and stay connected?
Is God finished working in my child’s life?
What mistakes can I bring to God and then release?
truth: If my children turn away from God, it does not automatically mean I failed. Even God’s children rebelled against Him. My children make their own choices. I can confess my mistakes, keep loving and praying for them, and trust that God is still at work. He welcomes prodigals home.
